name: 5000 Rummy
description: 5000 Rummy is a rummy card game that involves melding, sets, runs. The game originated in North America and has become popular worldwide.

overview.description: 5000 Rummy is a rummy card game that involves melding, sets, runs. The game originated in North America and has become popular worldwide.

history.origins: North American rummy; many house variants (no two descriptions agree). Named for common target score 5000; also played to 1500, 2000, 2500, 10000. Related to 500 Rummy but with different draw and scoring.

setup.players: 3–4 typically (2–8 with one or two decks). Deal and play clockwise.
setup.deck: 52 cards (3–4p); 104 (two packs) for 5–8p. Deal whole hands at once per player.
setup.dealing: Dealer gives each player their full hand before next player; first dealer by low card.
setup.equipment: Deck(s); score sheet to 5000 (or agreed target).

rules.objective: Be the first player to reach the target score (often 5000) by melding sets and runs and going out; opponents add deadwood to your score.
rules.gameplay: Deal full hands. Turn: draw one (from stock or multiple from discard pile, per variant), meld sets/runs if desired, discard one. Going out ends the round; others count deadwood against them. Round scores (or penalties) accumulate; first to target wins.
keyRules: Rummy melding; take from discard pile (one or several by variant)
Target score 5000 or other; going out ends round

strategy.basic: Meld early to lay off later; hold high cards for endgame; watch discard pile for 5000 Rummy.
strategy.intermediate: Count melds and deadwood; time when to go out; manage risk of being caught with high points.
strategy.advanced: Optimize meld order; bluff discards; track opponent targets (e.g. 5000).
tips: Going out ends the round; left-hand points count against others.

variations.name: Target score variants (1500–10000)
variations.description: Groups may play to alternative targets such as 1500, 2000, 2200, 2500, 2800 or 10000 instead of 5000; rules of play stay the same but the game length and pacing change with the chosen goal.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Target score differences affect only how long the game lasts; engine rules stay the same so no numeric overrides are modeled here.

variations.name: Permanent wild cards and jokers
variations.description: Some groups treat certain ranks (often twos) or added jokers as permanent wild cards worth high points, sometimes adjusting hand sizes or extra cards when a permanent wild appears as the upcard.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Wild card choices and exact point values vary widely between tables; engine keeps a generic wild-card capable model rather than hard-coding one specific set of overrides.

variations.name: George / 2500 Rummy (sets only)
variations.description: In the George / 2500 Rummy family, only sets of equal cards may be melded, runs are not allowed, and stricter conditions apply when taking multiple cards from the discard pile.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: This sets-only variant would need dedicated engine tuning for meld types and discard rules; it is documented here but not yet wired as a separate ruleset override.

scoring.description: Melded cards score points: aces and wild cards are typically worth 100 points each (or 200 when aces are wild); other picture cards and tens are 10 points; numeral cards 2–9 are 5 points. Unmelded cards left in hand at the end of a hand count against the player, and going out may award a bonus. Target score is often 5000, but many groups use 1500, 2000, 2200, 2500, 2800 or 10000.
scoring.winCondition: Be the first player to reach the target score (often 5000) by melding sets and runs and going out; opponents add deadwood to your score.
